topic: Mastering the Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Coordinate Systems as Languages
lecture_lines: Basis vectors form our coordinate language.
Changing basis changes the grid lines.
Positions are defined by relative basis units.
animations: 1. Create square grid #FFFFFF labeled 'Basis B'.
2. Show point 'Cat' at (4,4).
3. Transition to skewed grid #FFFF00 labeled 'Basis B''.
4. Maintain while updating values in 'Basis B''.
5. Highlight difference in coordinate representations.

sections.title: Defining the Transition Matrix
lecture_lines: Columns of P are new basis vectors.
animations: 1. Draw Set A in #FF0000, Set B in #00FF00.
2. Construct Matrix P with Set B vectors in terms of Set A.
3. Represent P as 'Bridge' connecting B to A.
4. Input v in B-coordinates into.
5. Display v in A-coordinates as output.

sections.title: The Mechanism: How to Calculate
lecture_lines: Step 2: Place them as columns in P.
Step 3: Multiply P by coordinate vector.
animations: 1. Display steps: '1. Identify B and B'', '2. Form P', '3. Calculate'.
2. Show 'Robot-Basis' vectors as columns forming P.
3. Illustrate P * [v_robot] = [v_world].
4. Show robot arm extending to [v_world].
5. Use checkmark for conversion.

sections.title: Summary & Geometric Intuition
lecture_lines: Change of basis is space relabelling.
The vector itself stays the same.
P-inverse converts back to original basis.
animations: 1. Split screen: point fixed, values change.
2. Animate 'Basis' rotation left, static coordinates.
3. Animate [x, y] values updating right for static point.
4. Introduce P^-1 reversing transformation.
5. Conclude: 'Same Point, Different Language'.
